title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's period conjecture for motives, tested on the simplest non-trivial abelian surface. Let C and C' be elliptic curves over a field k (embedded in C), both without complex multiplication and not isogenous to each other, and put A = C × C'.

The group G. G is the motivic Galois group, or Mumford–Tate group, of h^1(A). By Faltings/Serre-type results its identity component is {(g,g') in GL2 × GL2 : det g = det g'}. This group is isogenous to SL(2) × SL(2) × G_m and has dimension 3 + 3 + 1 = 7. The determinant must be shared because both curves give the same Tate twist (the Weil pairing / Legendre relation).

The group B. B is a Borel subgroup B(2) × B(2) × G_m of dimension 2 + 2 + 1 = 5. Most plausibly this is the stabilizer of the Hodge filtration F^1 ⊂ H^1_dR on each factor.

The argument. Some field K attached to A (presumably generated by periods or quasi-periods after a reduction of structure group to B) is controlled by a B-torsor. So trdeg_k K ≤ dim B = 5, and a fortiori trdeg over k(π) is ≤ 5. In brackets this is contrasted with the period-conjecture expectation: the period torsor of A is a G-torsor, so the field of periods should have transcendence degree dim G = 7 over k (for k algebraic). Over k(π) it should have dim G − 1 = 6, since 2πi accounts for the G_m factor.

Interpretation. The mismatch 5 versus 6 signals that the argument is flawed or the hypothesis is inconsistent. The NB ('Ceci ... pour une ... immersion k ⊂ C !') appears to locate the issue in the dependence on the chosen complex embedding of k. Transcendence statements about periods depend on the embedding. A reduction to B over k cannot hold for the Betti–de Rham comparison torsor, because the Hodge flag lives on the de Rham side only.

Bottom of page (upside down, struck out). This is unrelated scratch on topos-theoretic higher direct images: H^q(f)(X) = H^q(C/X, F), the cohomology of the induced (localized) site. In degree 0 it is H^0(C/X, F) = H^0(f)(X) for X in the site.

The page is a short exploratory test computation; much is illegible, so the identity of K is uncertain.
errors: Dimension counts are correct: dim G = 7, dim B = 5, and the expected transcendence degree over k(π) is 7 − 1 = 6.

The inference 'trdeg ≤ 5 over k, hence ≤ 5 over k(π)' is valid only as an upper bound. The contrast with 6 means the premise yielding K ⊂ (a B-torsor field) is incompatible with the period conjecture. Grothendieck's NB suggests he recognized that the premise depends on the embedding k ⊂ C, or is false as stated.
The handwriting is too unclear to be sure what K is; the reconstruction of the argument's premise is conjectural.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois / Mumford–Tate group of the product of two non-isogenous non-CM elliptic curves is isogenous to SL2×SL2×Gm, dim 7
ideas.modern_name: Mumford–Tate group of E×E' (Goursat lemma / Faltings isogeny theorem)

ideas.what: Period conjecture prediction: trdeg of the field of periods equals dim G, i.e. dim G − 1 over k(π)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966 footnote in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties'), developed by André
ideas.where_published: Publ. IHES 29 (1966), footnote; Lang's Introduction to Transcendental Numbers

ideas.what: Reduction of the period torsor to a Borel subgroup (Hodge flag) and a transcendence-degree bound by dim B
ideas.modern_name: Hodge filtration as parabolic reduction of the de Rham fibre functor; periods of the first kind

ideas.what: Higher direct images computed as cohomology of localized sites C/X
ideas.modern_name: R^q f_* via localization of topoi

deep.surprise_reason: This is a worked test case of the period conjecture for E×E' (dim 7, so 6 over k(π)) with a Borel-subgroup bound and a remark about embedding dependence. It shows Grothendieck testing his conjecture on explicit examples around 1970, which is historically nice but mathematically standard. The expected transcendence degree for products of elliptic curves is well known (Chudnovsky, Wüstholz, André).
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'C, C' courbes elliptiques sans mult. complexe, non isogènes' (the last word is hard to read).
'G ≃ (isogénie) Sl(2)×Sl(2)×G_m de dim 7' — the dimension is 7.
The bracket probably reads something like '[alors que l'on attend dim G − 1 = 6]'.
The NB reads roughly 'NB Ceci ... pour une ... immersion k ⊂ ℂ !'; the middle words (possibly 'faux'/'vrai' or 'toute'/'une') are illegible.
Upside-down bottom: '𝓗^q(f)(X) = H^q(C/X, F)' and 'H^q(C/X, F) ≃ ... H^0(C/X, F) [= 𝓗^0(f)(X) si X ∈ C]', all struck through.
